introduction.text: The Mausoleo di Lucilio Peto is a Roman burial monument located on the border of the Pincian Hill, notable for its late 1st‑century construction and its layered history of use and restoration.

history.description: Original construction during the middle to late Augustan age, likely in the late 1st century AD.
Second construction phase during the Trajanic age, adding a series of small hypogeal tombs.
Third phase in the 4th century AD, involving reuse of internal spaces and excavation of an ambulatory.
Fourth phase in the 16th century, when the marble façade was spoliated and the burial chamber was violated.
Discovery of the mausoleum in 1887 during construction of a retaining wall.
Evidence of occupation during the Second World War, with a tunnel appearing after 1940.
Restoration and reopening to the public in August 2010.

design.description: The mausoleum is a flat cylindrical tumulus with a 34‑metre diameter tambour built in opus quadratum and opus caementicium, covered in travertine, and featuring a dromos with a barrel vault leading to a cross‑shaped burial chamber.

art.description: An eastern arch bears a marble epigraph with a kyma lesbio, commemorating M. Lucilius Paetus.
